_meta.purpose: Verifiable structural facts about the reference carriers and the North American trucking market, used to ground generated content and to catch invented numbers.
_meta.as_of: 2025 public filings and industry sources; verify before quoting externally

segments.name: Intermodal
segments.description: Company-owned 53-foot containers moved on BNSF and Norfolk Southern rail, with J.B. Hunt drayage on both ends. The largest intermodal container fleet in North America, roughly 120,000 containers.
segments.note: Historic BNSF partnership dating to 1989, the first major intermodal alliance between a truckload carrier and a Class I railroad. Eastern network runs with Norfolk Southern.

segments.name: Dedicated Contract Services
segments.description: Long-term contracts where J.B. Hunt operates a customer-dedicated private fleet, typically 3-7 year terms with the customer's branding on equipment.
segments.note: Includes private fleet conversion, where a shipper outsources an in-house fleet

segments.name: Integrated Capacity Solutions
segments.description: Non-asset freight brokerage operating on the J.B. Hunt 360 platform, matching shipper freight to third-party carrier capacity.

segments.name: Final Mile Services
segments.description: Big and bulky home delivery of appliances, furniture and fitness equipment, including threshold, room-of-choice and white-glove installation service levels, run from a network of cross-dock hubs.

segments.name: Truckload
segments.description: Asset-light dry van truckload including the 360box drop-trailer program.

platform.name: J.B. Hunt 360
platform.description: Proprietary multimodal marketplace connecting shippers and carriers across all segments; 360box is the drop-trailer capacity product.

secondary_archetype.note: Orange tractors are the company's best-known identifier. Rail partners include Union Pacific and CSX. Operates one of the larger battery-electric Class 8 fleets in the US through its Freightliner eCascadia deployment in Southern California. Used here as a reference point where J.B. Hunt's model does not cover a process well - for example company-owned driving academies and Power Only brokerage.
